 Graphic: Andrew Hamilton/UAA Communications The Opening Kickoff: No. 24 Gators vs. Vanderbilt — Momentum Into Home Finale
 Friday, November 20, 2026 | Football, Scott Carter
 Share: By: Scott Carter, Senior Writer 
 Florida Notes | Vanderbilt Notes | UF Game Day | Broadcast Information 
GAINESVILLE, Fla. — When the Gators burst from their locker room and onto Spurrier-Florida Field for the final home game of the season on Saturday, it will mark 77 days since Gators coach Jon Sumrall first experienced the sensation.
In his UF debut, Sumrall's inaugural Gators team scored a season-high 66 points to hammer FAU. The victory launched a four-game win streak that included a road win at Auburn and a home upset of Ole Miss. The victories earned Florida an avalanche of praise as it climbed to No. 8 in the national rankings.
And then a road loss at Missouri dampened the enthusiasm, followed by a 19-point homecoming loss to South Carolina that left Ben Hill Stadium half-empty by the end of the game.
"This has been the most up-and-down [team] I've been around," Sumrall said this week. "The inconsistency has driven me crazy."
Florida rebounded by pulling off a surprise victory at Texas, but barely made a whimper in losses to Georgia and Oklahoma, sparking a loud round of noise in the system. But once again, the Gators pulled themselves from the turf and upset No. 13 Kentucky on the road.
The Gators (6-4, 4-4) became bowl-eligible with the victory and look to finish strong at home Saturday against Vanderbilt (4-6, 1-6) as they close the Southeastern Conference schedule.
 24 straight sellouts ✅ https://t.co/BdK9HJisLU
— Florida Gators Football (@GatorsFB) November 20, 2026 
In his fifth season as a head coach, Sumrall won't take his team to the conference championship game for the first time, but that doesn't mean he lacks important goals as the season winds down.
He jumped on the Gators at practice on Wednesday for their lack of urgency. He said they responded accordingly after he turned into a maniac, but he longs for the day such reminders are not necessary.
"We haven't handled success well at times this year, and it's been a real frustration," Sumrall said. "We've got to grow up and be more mature, more disciplined and pay greater attention to detail. Complacency is a killer, and you can't fall into the relief of 'You got a win last week, so it has nothing to do with this week.' You always have to be urgent and strain."
Florida has its final opportunity to showcase that mentality at home when the Commodores pay a visit.
 Here is our latest edition of The Opening Kickoff for a closer look at the Florida-Vanderbilt game:
 THREE STORYLINES 
 With the Gators bowl-eligible for the first time since 2024 — they beat Sumrall's Tulane team in the Gasparilla Bowl — they are in the postseason conversation. As bowl-projection season grows by the hour, most projections have the Gators staying in the Sunshine State, either in the ReliaQuest Bowl in Tampa, the Citrus Bowl in Orlando or the Gator Bowl in Jacksonville. It makes sense the Gators would stay close to home, but there are a lot of games left and the standings are in flux. If Florida can beat Vanderbilt and Florida State to close the season and win a bowl game, it would be the program's first nine-win season since 2019.
 Aaron Philo is back in charge for the Gators after regaining the starting quarterback job at Kentucky. Philo passed for 119 yards and ran for 102 to keep Florida moving the chains in the second half of their 21-14 win over the Wildcats, Florida's first win in Lexington since 2019. Philo made his most impressive plays on the ground, rushing for 26 of the final 29 yards on the Gators' go-ahead drive.
 Florida can clinch a winning SEC record with a victory, a feat it has not accomplished since 2020. The Gators are 4-4 in SEC play and can strengthen their bowl position in Sumrall's first season. Florida entered the season 14-26 in conference play over the past five seasons, so a winning league record is a step in the right direction for a program that had lost 27 of 50 games when Sumrall was hired.
 THREE PLAYERS TO WATCH 
 Jadan Baugh ( see below ) is closing in on another 1,000-yard rushing season. Baugh moved closer by rushing for 69 yards on 18 carries at Kentucky. Baugh has found yards difficult to come by in the past six games after piling up 600 in the first four games. The Commodores rank 11th in the SEC in rushing defense (133.2 yards per game) and have allowed only one 100-yard rusher: Delaware's Jo Silver (16 carries, 109 yards).
 Commodores true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis has started seven games and completed 170 of 264 passes (64.4%) for 1,880 yards, eight touchdowns and eight interceptions. The 6-foot-3, 230-pound Curtis arrived at Vanderbilt as the highest-rated recruit in program history. Curtis was the 2025 Tennessee Gatorade Player of the Year and the No. 1-rated quarterback in the 2026 recruiting class out of Nashville Christian School.
 Gators sophomore edge rusher Jayden Woods continues to improve. He ranks third on the team with 43 tackles and has four quarterback hurries and two forced fumbles. Curtis threw 40 times in last week's loss to Alabama and was sacked five times. Curtis has fumbled six times, losing four, so Woods and Co. have an opportunity to rattle the young quarterback if they can get consistent pressure.
 FIVE QUESTIONS WITH … GATORS CB BEN HANKS III 
 A sophomore cornerback, Hanks had a career-high seven tackles at Kentucky and played all 53 defensive snaps. His father is former UF standout Ben Hanks, a four-year letterman from 1992-95. 
 Cornerback Ben Hanks III breaks up a fourth-down pass in last week's 21-14 victory at Kentucky. (Photo: Cassie Baker /UAA Communications) 
 Q: What did you see on that fourth-down pass breakup against Kentucky? 
A: First of all, I would just say, going into that drive, I was expecting to get back on defense. I wanted to be that spark on the defense. So, just going into that drive, that first down was an incomplete pass. Second down was a shot at me, had the ball tipped by J. Woods. And third down came, I was like, 'I gotta make a play,' and then fourth down came. We went on man, came back over, see the tight end. I know that was one of their best players, so they'll try to attack him, and I just sat on it and tried to take the ball away from him and ended up with an incomplete pass.
 Q: What's the growth process been like in your first year as a starter? 
A: I'd say definitely been ups and downs in my situation I'm in right now. But I mean, I learned from a lot of it. It's been a great obstacle, but just going into every week as a new mindset to get better and make new plays. That's really my mindset.
 Q: What's it like having a father who played here? 
A: We talk every day after practice, after each game, the good, the ugly, the bad. So I mean, he talks to me in my ear, just telling me to keep going, stay level-headed, stay with the process. Everything's gonna play out.
 Q: How is the communication defensively after some struggles early? 
A: I'd say that's a big part of our game we grew at. So, I mean, just learning from that part was amazing. Just learning the defense, learning everything going together was a big part of the situation we was in. We all bought in, came together, and it's showing on the field.
 Q: What's the season been like from a player's perspective? 
A: We all want a winning season. We still in a winning season, but we all came in with a 4-0 record and the mindset of we trying to win every game,'so just going in there every game, just trying to compete, trying to play better and play for the people that's in front of you or next to you.
 THREE DIGITS 
 95 —  Yards rushing Gators running back Jadan Baugh needs to become the first player in school history with back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons.
 7 — First-year SEC coaches since 1990 to beat at least three teams ranked in the AP Top 25. With last week's win at No. 13 Kentucky, Florida's Jon Sumrall joined Nick Saban (2000, LSU), Urban Meyer (2005, Florida), Les Miles (2005, LSU), Gus Malzahn (2013, Auburn), Dan Mullen (2018, Florida) and Kalen DeBoer (2024, Alabama).
 24 — Tackles Florida linebacker Myles Graham needs to become the first UF player since linebacker David Reese to have 100 tackles in a season. Reese, currently a Gators defensive quality control analyst, had 102 tackles in 2017.
 AVAILABILITY REPORT* 
 FLORIDA — OUT: WR Vernell Brown III (knee), LB Jaden Robinson (undisclosed), TE Lacota Dippre (ankle), S DJ Coleman (ankle), OL Emeka Ugorji (ankle), CB Dijon Johnson (undisclosed). PROBABLE:  S Bryce Thornton (undisclosed), WR Bailey Stockton (foot).  VANDERBILT — OUT:  CB Cobey Sellers, QB Blaze Berlowitz, DE Edwin Kolenge, LB Josiah Broxton, RB Evan Hampton, LB Daniel Vollmer Jr., OL Gunner Givens, DL Aaron Bryant, OL Ted Gregoire.
*Updated Saturday morning
 NEWS, NOTES, NUGGETS 
 The Gators and Commodores renew their rivalry for the first time since 2023. Florida leads the all-time series 44-11-2, including 24-2-1 at home.
 Florida climbed back into the AP Top 25 this week at No. 23 following last week's win at Kentucky. It's the third time this season Florida has entered the poll after not being ranked the previous week, a first in program history.
 The Gators had lost 14 consecutive away games against ranked opponents before beating No. 7 Texas last month. Following their win at No. 13 Kentucky, the Gators won back-to-back road games while unranked for the first time since the 2003 season.
 UF head coach Jon Sumrall has been bowl-eligible in each of his five seasons as a head coach, twice at Troy, twice at Tulane and now in his first season at Florida.
 Running back Jadan Baugh 's 15 rushing touchdowns rank second on the program's single-season list behind Tim Tebow 's 23 during his Heisman Trophy-winning season in 2007.
 The Gators' secondary took another hit with starting safety DJ Coleman out against the Commodores. Coleman has started all 10 games and is fourth on the team with 42 tackles and a team-leading two interceptions. Fellow safety Bryce Thornton , who did not play at Kentucky, has been upgraded to probable. Lagonza Hayward , Alfonzo Allen Jr. , Kanye Clark and Cam Dooley picked up additional reps at Kentucky.
 Safety DJ Coleman is listed as unavailable for Saturday's game. (Photo: Victoria Riccobono /UAA Communications) 
 The Gators own the toughest SEC schedule heading into their final conference game. Florida's SEC opponents are a combined 32-21 for a .604 winning percentage. No other SEC team has played a conference schedule with opponents winning at a .600 clip.
 Florida edge rusher Jayden Woods had 1.5 sacks at Kentucky to give him a team-high six on the season. Woods also leads the Gators with 10 tackles for loss.
 Vanderbilt junior quarterback Whit Muschamp is the son of former Gators head coach Will Muschamp . He made his collegiate debut last season against Georgia State and is 2-for-2 for 18 yards this season, his only appearance coming against Georgia, his dad's alma mater.
 Commodores senior receiver Junior Sherrill , who grew up in Nashville, has caught a pass in 47 consecutive games, the longest active streak among FBS players. Sherrill's streak is the longest for a Vanderbilt player since 1996.
 CHARTING THE GATORS 
 Jadan Baugh 
Gators running back Jadan Baugh is attempting to become the first UF player with official back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons. Thanks to SaturdayDownSouth.com 's extensive SEC rushing database , we compiled each current SEC program's last back-to-back 1,000-yard rusher.
Meanwhile, in a quirky NCAA rule during former Gators running back Emmitt Smith 's career, he officially rushed for 988 yards as a sophomore in 1988. Smith, who went on to become the NFL's all-time leading rusher, still owns the top two single-season rushing marks in program history (1,599 yards in 1989 and 1,341 in 1987).
While he rushed for 159 yards and was named MVP of the 1988 All-American Bowl, the performance is not included in Smith's injury-marred sophomore season total. Instead of 1,147 yards in the record book, the 988 stands.

 THEY SAID IT 
 "A senior citizen day. He'll have a retirement party is what he's having. He would love to keep playing football after this year, obviously. But I know it won't be here because there are rules about how long you can play, allegedly." — Gators head coach Jon Sumrall on seventh-year receiver Kahleil Jackson being honored on Senior Day
 "Florida is a special experience. It's tighter, a little more vertical. And again, that's a proud fan base that makes it challenging, but it's also, you know, these are the things you want." — Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea on playing at The Swamp
 "This last month that we've been playing football we're playing a lot more aggressive. Effort is not a question. You see guys playing hard, playing with a lot of effort. That's what we want our defense to be about." — Gators linebacker Aaron Chiles on defensive turnaround 
 THEY WROTE IT 
 Gators' Senior Day isn't what it used to be amid college football's changing era, writes Edgar Thompson of the Orlando Sentinel .
 Florida head coach Jon Sumrall explains his outburst toward offensive line coach Phil Trautwein at the end of the Kentucky game, writes Kevin Brockway of the Gainesville Sun .
 Vanderbilt is fighting flags and foes in quest to become bowl-eligible, writes John Glennon of the Nashville Post .
 WHY GATORS WILL WIN 
They maintain the momentum they built in the second half of their comeback win at Kentucky. That means getting off to a better start than a week ago and continuing to rely on quarterback Aaron Philo 's dual-threat ability. Defensively, get the Commodores off the field, let the offense build a lead, and pump up the crowd in the final home game. Oh, and stop committing so many penalties, especially those on the opening drive at Kentucky that proved to be drive killers.
 WHY COMMODORES WILL WIN 
They repeat the formula South Carolina and Oklahoma used: grab an early lead, control possession, win the turnover battle and force the Gators out of their comfort zone. Florida committed five turnovers without a takeaway in home losses to the Gamecocks and Sooners. A certain good sign for the Commodores will be if they can run the ball to sustain drives. They rank last in the SEC in rushing (102.1 yards per game), with Sedrick Alexander (360 yards, 4.0 per carry) as their top backfield threat.
